searchText: I have written an EIP that bumps the difficulty bomb one more (last?) time but looking at Muir Glacier, I'm wondering why the inflation schedule was not adjusted. Was there any discussion around that or was it just omitted to prevent controversy? Given that we are moving to proof-of-stake inflation, we should carefully look into the proof-of-work issuance. <vbuterin> I guess the community felt that at the time 2 eth was safe enough and it was not sufficiently clear that less than 2 eth is safe? <vbuterin> The next de-facto issuance decrease (EIP 1559) will ironically enough bring total mining rewards back down from ~3.5 to 2 😂😂 I remember the debate around 2 ETH, my question was if there was a similar debate when considering Muir Glacier that I'm not aware of maybe. <vbuterin> I don't think there was much debate Ok <vbuterin> Primarily because no one tried to seriously push for a decrease <jhancock76> There was little discussion. <jhancock76> They were looked as independents problems at the time, imo. The delay of the ice age was to return block times to normal. <jhancock76> The issuance wasn’t a priority at the time. <vbuterin> right, though it *is* true that issuance reductions have historically been done simultaneously with ice ages I don't think there was ever a particularly *good* reason to do issuance reduction at the same time as ice age pushes though. Even when you do the issuance reduction after the ice age bomb lands, it still is a pretty weak argument. Along the lines of, "we accidentally decreased inflation for a few months, that means that we should leave inflation at that rate permanently". Really there wasn't enough time to have a real discussion on what issuance should be when Muir Glacier was proposed. If we had put it in with Istanbul and discussed it for 6 months I bet it would have happened. My perspective is 1559 fee burn could serve as the next ice age reward reduction. But bringing the reward back to 5 is a non-starter. I think the original premise was something along the lines of "the difficulty bomb was supposed to get us to Eth2, which has lower issuance. because we're going to be late shipping Eth2, we should somewhat compensate people who had an expectation of lowered issuance, so let's reduce the supply". Worth noting that in the <#798586271445680129> channel, a lot of folks are claiming that the 3->2 issuance was somehow linked to a soft promise of ProgPow going live, and they were obviously frustrated when that didn't happen.
